newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish parliament to reopen after summer recess.
newsitem.headline: Turkish parliament to reopen after summer recess.

text.p: Turkish President Suleyman Demirel was to address the start of a new parliament session on Tuesday after a two-month summer recess, parliamentary officials said.

Demirel will give a speech to the 550-seat assembly at 1500 (1200 GMT). The main opposition Motherland Party (ANAP) has promised to toughen its criticism of Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's Islamist-led government in the months ahead.
ANAP leaders met at a mountain resort in western Turkey at the weekend to find a way to bring down the three-month-old coalition through censure motions against ministers.
The alliance of Erbakan's Welfare Party with the conservative True Path Party (DYP) of pro-West Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller has 279 MPs, four more than the number needed to defeat a censure motion.
The government also has the tepid backing of seven deputies from a small far-right group.
